attempt: ONE. No retry, no second prompt variant, and no tuning after any eval output is seen. **The attempt is SPENT at the first GOLD-row reply generated** — not at pod create, not at a dev reply, and not at the dev gate, whose 200 rows are labelled comments outside both the sealed fourteen and the eval pack's sixty-four. A session that closes before any gold row is answered has NOT spent it and returns to the team lead, and every rung before rung 8 closes the session in exactly that state
authority: the operator's rulings of 2026-08-20 registered in docs/STATUS.md «Открытые решения» п. 0 — the base stays Gemma-4-31B, the operator's word replaces sitting C, the goal is the analysis of docs/REFERENCE-signals-w1.md, and the team lead labels — plus the three answers of the joint step review: dev-200, the shot in the same session on a pre-registered gate, and the dev gate as written below

loss_budget.rule: a refusal and an ABSENT row cost exactly what a disagreement costs. The budget is registered before the run so the result cannot be re-read against one nobody wrote

P1_per_comment_agreement.rule: the sealed r2 gold, answered under probe-b's own 64-unit pack identity. ONE attempt, SPENT at the first gold-row reply

census_50.reading: the subject_type distribution v2 answers the eval pack's census rows with, beside the base's and arm A's. Line B's whole finding was a census that moved while the bar did not (None 25 → 9, не_наш_рынок 8 → 23)
census_50.rule: OBSERVATION ONLY — no number here moves any gate

dev_gate.reachability: our_v2 ≤ 49, so the delta is unreachable whenever our_base > 39. That is a STOP, not a RED: the gate could not have been met by any v2 whatever, the attempt is NOT spent, and the table goes to the operator with the reading
dev_gate.rule: paired on the same 200 rows: our_v2 − our_base ≥ 10 (correct rows among the 49 категория_личное/молочный_бренд labels) AND agree_v2 − agree_base ≥ -5 (over all 200). BOTH or no shot
dev_gate.the_base_is_measured_here: the base's dev numbers are MEASURED in this session on the same pod, never assumed and never taken from another run. That is what «paired» means
dev_gate.when: rung 7, before the shot, on the Mac

judge.absent_or_refusal: a DISAGREEMENT — silence about a row that was asked is a miss
judge.rule: the same bytes probe-b and lora-b were scored with. A new equality loop would be a second definition of the bar and is refused

do_not: no training, no adapter, no second prompt variant, no tuning after any eval output
never edit results/prereg_pass1_probe_b.json, results/pass1_probe_b_pack.json, the gold, the labels or the base verdict
never touch the sealed fourteen before the dev gate says GO
never leave --watch while a pod is billing

rows.formula: boot + dev base + dev v2 + shot + overhead
rows.name: total_seconds

rows.formula: hard stop at the ceiling < cap
rows.name: the_hard_stop_is_under_the_cap

rows.formula: worst case at the ceiling < cap
rows.name: the_worst_case_is_under_the_cap

rows.formula: 450.0 s ≥ max(every boot this stack has measured) = 353.0 s
rows.name: boot_ceiling_over_the_worst_measured_boot

rows.formula: all 49 «our» labels + 151 stratified from the other 601
rows.name: dev_rows

rows.formula: probe-b's eval pack, unchanged in identity and order
rows.name: shot_units

rows.formula: 49 «our» rows − 10 = the highest base that leaves it open
rows.name: our_delta_is_reachable_at_the_bases_own_worst

h6.rule: every number docs/PROMPT-pass1-fewshot.md prints, re-derived from the formula the contract names for it. `equals` allows 1% — a rounding is not a finding; `rounds_to` is for the two figures the contract prints rounded; `below` and `at_least` check the DIRECTION of a margin, which is what a ceiling has instead of a value

transport.rule: it CALLS scripts/pass1_pod_runner.py, which calls the shipped v5 runner. One model load serves every leg of a pack, and each leg is answered into its own out-file

v2_is_v1_plus_two_paragraphs.rule: PASS1_COMMENT_PROMPT_V2 == PASS1_COMMENT_PROMPT + the clause + the slot, and nothing else. tests/test_pass1_prompt.py asserts it in both directions

kill_clock.read: costPerHr in the create response is the meter of record (Dv448)
kill_clock.rule: live price > $0.8/h at create → STOP, no endpoint. The backstop stamp is checked against the cumulative hard stop in the same command
ssh dead-man ≤ 180 s or KILL — pass1-probe's proven gate-0
boot → first reply ≤ 450 s or KILL. The ceiling is above every boot this stack has measured, the worst of them 353 s

kill_clock.before: the run is allowed to continue past a call
kill_clock.rule: projection gate every 20 calls: the projected attempt total at MEASURED rates, with every leg still owed priced, must fit the cap at the LIVE price AND the cumulative hard stop, else KILL

kill_clock.read: held by scripts/gate_pass1_fewshot.py --watch, a BLOCKING loop
kill_clock.rule: liveness: 600 s with no new answered row and no new pod-log line → KILL. The deadline is measured from the LAST EVENT and never from create. The executor does not poll by hand and does not leave the loop — lora-b lost 9 720 s and an arm because every rung there watched the training log and none watched a pod that had stopped working

kill_clock.read: the `--terminate-after` stamp, read back and refused on overshoot
kill_clock.rule: cumulative hard stop 6300 s, PLATFORM-held. Each pod's --terminate-after is its own create plus what the stop has left

kill_clock.read: bars.dev_gate — both inequalities, paired on the same 200 rows
kill_clock.rule: dev gate: our_v2 − our_base ≥ 10 AND agree_v2 − agree_base ≥ -5. Both or NO shot. RED → delete, prove it by listing, the attempt is NOT spent, and the table returns to the team lead
the shot is 64 units into its OWN out-file, never a dev leg's — the shipped resume skips every id it already sees (Dv560). The attempt is SPENT at the first gold-row reply

arithmetic.boot_rule: the registered ceiling, and rung 3's own threshold. It is ≥ the worst boot this stack has measured (353.0 s, lora-b) by ×1.2748. The contract's parenthetical «worst 293 × 1.5» quotes the worst as it stood before lora-b measured 353 s; the CEILING has not moved and is still above the true worst

cumulative.hard_stop_rule: cumulative billed ≤ 1.75 h = $1.4 at the $0.8/h ceiling. It sits UNDER the $1.50 cap it defends, and it is the PLATFORM that enforces it — so it protects even a hung call no gate can see

projection_gate.formula: billed_by_closed_pods + elapsed_on_this_pod + Σ over every leg still owed of (its remaining calls × its s/call) + overhead_seconds. A leg with a reply is priced at its MEASURED rate — the larger of its mean and its last call; a leg with none is priced at the LARGER of its registered rate and the worst rate measured on this pod so far
projection_gate.verdict: KILL if the projection exceeds $1.50 at the LIVE price, or exceeds the 6300 s hard stop in seconds. The stricter binds
projection_gate.why_every_leg: the shot's 64 calls are what makes the dev legs affordable at all. A projection that priced only the running leg would open a run the cap closes

cumulative.rule: the hard stop and EVERY budget check count across ALL pods of this attempt, never per pod. `--terminate-after` on each pod is stamped at that pod's create plus the hard stop LESS what every closed pod already billed, so two pods cannot each be given a fresh window
cumulative.session_ceiling_rule: cap / price ceiling — the longest session the cap can pay for

arithmetic.overhead_rule: 0.5 h — staging, the scp's, the dev gate on the Mac, and the deletion

seconds_per_call.rule: base is MEASURED — probe-b's 64 paid calls on an RTX 4090, mean 5.162 s. v2 is UNMEASURED and is registered as a BOUND: 1.5 × the measured base, for the longer prefill five labelled examples add. Rung 4 measures it at call 20 and every 20 after that, and the projection then prices the rest at what the pod is actually doing
seconds_per_call.sample: results/pass1_probe_b_rows.jsonl — 64 calls, one card, one boot. Named beside the number because a rate is a property of the sample it was measured on

money.cap_rule: $1.50 all-in, frozen at the FIRST `pod create`. Raising it is the operator's word BEFORE any endpoint exists, never after a reading
money.guard: PYTHONPATH=src python3.11 scripts/runpod_guard.py --step pass1-fewshot --step-cap 1.50 — the anchor is committed BEFORE the pod exists, and the reading is what the rungs that name one act on

meter.card_preferred: probe-b's class — RTX 4090 at $0.74/h, the card the 5.162 s/call sample was measured on. An A6000 under the ceiling is allowed
meter.datacenter: EU-RO-1, pinned by network volume qw4nwleanc — the volume decides
meter.memory: this line does NOT train, so lora-b's 48 GB constraint does not apply: probe-b served this same base on a 24 GB 4090. That makes rung 1 a price gate against a much wider market than lora-b faced
meter.price_rule: **READ ON THE DAY.** `costPerHr` in the create response is the meter of record and every figure here is recomputed from it by rung 4 before the run is allowed to continue
meter.resource: ONE rented pod, billed for every second it EXISTS — from `pod create` to `pod delete`. `pod stop` does not stop the bill, so the run deletes and never stops

reading.rule: money is read from the GUARD, never from a ledger and never from prose (Dv33)

recovery.rule: ONE pod re-creation, and only after a deletion PROVEN by listing. It happens only if the guard READING plus the worst case remaining at MEASURED rates is ≤ $1.50 and inside the cumulative stop. Never two billing endpoints
recovery.there_is_no_generation_checkpoint_to_los: every reply is flushed to its out-file as it lands and the shipped resume skips every unit already answered, so a re-creation re-asks only what has no reply. That is the one thing this line has that lora-b did not: a KILL mid-leg costs the boot, not the leg

multiplicity: this is the THIRD shot at the same fourteen — the base (pass1-probe-b), arm A (lora-b) and now v2 — so the false-pass odds are about 3p and not p. Named here, in the registration, so the verdict is never read as a single shot. Accepted by the operator's «приступаем» of 2026-08-20

holdout.rule: registered EVALUATION ONLY before this session. This line trains nothing, so dev rows MAY overlap it and the overlap is published in both records

sealed_source.identity_and_order: unchanged — asserted id by id, in order
sealed_source.rule: the sealed pack, the sealed base verdict and the gold are READ and never written. The base is not re-run on the fourteen: its answers are the ones results/pass1_probe_b_verdict.json already holds

return_to_the_operator: **A FAILED BAR GOES BACK TO THE OPERATOR, never to a prompt iteration.** A RED dev gate or a RED shot closes this line in-session: nothing is re-worded, nothing is re-run, and the dev table and the per-row fourteen go back for the next option of the menu (synthetic + LoRA, or rationale-supervised LoRA). A GREEN shot ships v2 as the pass-1 prompt of the window run, which is the NEXT contract and is priced there
what_this_line_is: line B (labels + LoRA) closed RED: the adapter learned the label marginal and not the decision. All four «категория» misses of the base are ONE error class — the comment MENTIONS a retailer or a brand inside a category habit, and the base classifies by the mention. This line fixes the DEFINITION in the prompt and shows the contrast with labelled neighbours. Nothing is trained
